Investigate ONLY files under $EPISODE_ROOT — do not read anything elsewhere on the filesystem, and there is no answer key or solution to find; solve it yourself.

A Python 3.11 service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service depends on roughly thirty distributions
installed into $EPISODE_ROOT/site-packages. During an egress review several
outbound connection attempts were seen going to hosts that are not the organisation's
internal mirror and appear nowhere in the first-party source under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/src; the
review notes are at $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/logs/egress.log. The intended, resolved dependency set
is pinned in $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/requirements.lock, the internal mirror at $EPISODE_ROOT/opt/mirror holds the
trusted builds of the organisation's own packages, a CycloneDX SBOM is at
$EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/sbom.cdx.json, local modifications the platform team has approved are
recorded in $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/PATCHES.md, and each installed distribution carries a dist-info
RECORD integrity manifest.

More than one distribution has been compromised through the supply chain, and they were
not all compromised the same way. Some other distributions in the environment look
irregular but are benign, and those must not be reported as compromised.

Write a findings report as a single JSON object at the absolute path $EPISODE_ROOT/app/report.json
with exactly one key, "compromised", whose value is a JSON array holding one object per
genuinely compromised distribution and nothing else. Each object must have these keys:
  package   - the distribution name
  vector    - the compromise mechanism, one of: tampered-file, malicious-wheel,
              dependency-confusion, typosquat, install-hook
  trigger   - when the injected code first runs, one of: import, install,
              runtime-entrypoint, interpreter-startup
  cwe       - the CWE identifier (form "CWE-###") that most precisely classifies the
              weakness
  owasp     - the OWASP Top 10 2021 category identifier (form "A##:2021")
  indicator - the primary indicator of compromise recovered from disk: the
              fully-qualified host the code contacts where it beacons, otherwise the
              single most specific artefact identifying the compromise (a malicious
              version string, an impersonated package name, or the module executed at
              startup)

Then remediate the environment so that every compromised distribution is neutralised —
restored to its trusted build, repinned to the trusted source, or removed — while the
benign distributions are left in place and the service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service still imports
and runs unchanged. The environment has no outbound network access; recover every
reported value from the files on disk alone.

## Findings — 9 compromised distributions, 5 distinct vectors

| Package | Vector | Trigger | CWE | Indicator (beacon host) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| geoindex | tampered-file | import | CWE-506 | sync-metrics.geoindex-cdn.net |
| logkit | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-507 | logkit-metrics.telemetry-cdn.net |
| metricslib | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-507 | collector.metricslib-telemetry.io |
| svc-cli | malicious-wheel | runtime-entrypoint | CWE-507 | svc-cli-collect.pkg-telemetry.net |
| buildtools-ext | install-hook | interpreter-startup | CWE-912 | bt-ext-beacon.buildcdn.net |
| corp-telemetry | dependency-confusion | import | CWE-427 | corp-telemetry-public.s3-collector.net |

| sluglfy | typosquat | import | CWE-829 | sluglfy-collect.pkgcdn.net |
| urllib33 | typosquat | import | CWE-829 | urllib33-telemetry.pkgcdn.net |

All nine are OWASP **A08:2021** (Software and Data Integrity Failures).

**How each was separated from the others:** `geoindex/_grid.py` was the only payload whose dist-info RECORD hash *mismatched* — injected after install. `logkit`, `metricslib` and `svc-cli` had RECORDs self-consistent with their malicious content but diverged from `opt/mirror`'s trusted builds — the wheels shipped compromised (metricslib gained an entire `_agg.py` backend with an XOR-obfuscated host, `m3tr1c` key). `corp-telemetry` and `metrics-core` are internal-index-only names installed at version **9.9.9** with `INSTALLER: pypi-public`, shadowing the pinned 1.4.2/2.0.0. `sluglfy`/`urllib33` are lookalikes of `slugify`/`urllib3`, also `pypi-public`, and absent from the lock. `buildtools_ext_autoload.pth` was the single file on disk covered by *no* RECORD — an install-time drop that runs `buildtools_ext._bootstrap` before any import, matching the egress log's pre-import connection.

**Ruled benign and left untouched:** `crashreporter` and `debug_shell` (loopback-only, latter off by default), `vendored_min` and `fastserialize` (base64/`exec`/`marshal` over local first-party source, no network), `oldcrypto` (SBOM CVE — vulnerable, not tampered), `localpatch_ui` (RECORD mismatch approved in PATCHES.md).

## Remediation

Restored `geoindex`, `logkit`, `metricslib` from `opt/mirror` (RECORDs regenerated); reinstalled `corp-telemetry` 1.4.2 and `metrics-core` 2.0.0 from the mirror, deleting the 9.9.9 public builds; deleted the `.pth` autoloader and `_bootstrap.py`; deleted `svc_cli/_hooks.py` and its `svc-report` console-script entry point.

Verification: every RECORD now validates except `localpatch_ui` (the approved patch), all 53 lock pins are installed at the pinned version, every remaining `INSTALLER` reads `internal-mirror`, and a filesystem sweep for the nine IOCs (plaintext and base64) returns zero hits. The service runs unchanged with `socket.create_connection`/`urlopen` trip-wired — no egress, `run()` returns `9q9hyh053`.

One judgment call worth your review: `src/svc/net.py` and `src/svc/shim.py` import the typosquat names directly, so deleting those distributions outright would break the service, which you required to keep running unchanged. I removed both typosquat packages and their dist-info, and left first-party alias modules `site-packages/sluglfy.py` / `site-packages/urllib33.py` that re-export from the trusted `slugify` / `urllib3` — no payload, no dist-info.
